sections.name: File setup, MoneyHit
sections.title: Money word list and negation rule
sections.what: Defines the list of money words and symbols that count as a problem, and the pattern that recognises a negation word before them.
sections.why: Keeps the word list and the disclaimer exception together so both audits use the same definition.
sections.watch_out: Both the unit and the browser audits import this list, so a change here changes both.

sections.name: findMoneyTerms
sections.title: Finding money words in text
sections.what: Searches a block of text and returns each money word that is not inside a 'no money' disclaimer, with its surrounding context.
sections.why: Reports only real problems, so a legitimate statement like no entry fees does not fail the audit.
sections.watch_out: The context is trimmed to forty characters on each side, so a reviewer may need to open the page to judge a hit.

summary: Scans visible page text for money-related words and reports only those that are not part of a 'no money' disclaimer.
purpose: Enforces the product rule that the app must not look like it handles money, for example payments, prizes, or betting.
why: The app is meant to be free of money features, so a stray word like pay or prize on a page would be a product problem as well as a wording problem.
how: It holds one pattern that lists many money words and symbols. For each match it looks at the text just before the word; if a negation word such as no, never, or without appears close before it, the match is skipped. It also skips a payment-policy setting that shows as a special marker. Every other match is recorded with a short piece of surrounding text so a reviewer can see the context.
inputs: A label for where the text came from, such as a page path, and the visible text of that page.
outputs: A list of hits. Each hit has the label, the matched word, and about forty characters of context on each side.
risks: The negation check only looks back about forty characters and stops at sentence punctuation, so an unusual phrasing like a disclaimer far from the word could be reported as a false alarm. A real money word after a negation word in the same clause would be missed.
debug: If a page fails, read the reported context to see whether the word is real or a disclaimer. For a false alarm, adjust the wording on the page or extend the negation rule. Check the word list if a legitimate word is being flagged.
